newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate down, baht steady late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate down, baht steady late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank fell to 13.50-14.00 percent late on Monday from 14.00-14.50 percent in the morning, dealers said.
Dealers said the money supply was slighly easier from the morning, but high demand for funds by some finance firms hindered the interbank rate from falling further.
"Demand for funds by finance firms remained strong today. Banks were still reluctant to lend to most finance firms due to concerns about the recent rumour," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

A rumour that some finance firms had liquidity problems after their clients had defaulted on margin loans battered the stock market on Friday. The Bank of Thailand and Stock Exchange of Thailand denied the rumours.
The baht was steady at 25.345-25.348 to the dollar in late trade compared with 25.340-25.350, dealers said.

"The dollar/baht spot rate was still high due to the hangover of the baht devaluation rumour from Friday," said one currecy dealer at a foreign bank. "But the market was quiet because people think it was expensive to buy dollars right now."

A rumour of a possible baht devaluation, which emerged late on Friday morning in Singapore, sparked heavy selling of the Thai unit for the dollar, dealers said. The Bank of Thailand denied the market talk about possible baht devaluation.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium rose further to 11.25/12.25 satangs per dollar from 10.00/11.00 on lingering concern on the market rumour about possible baht devaluation, dealers said.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.33 to the dollar against 25.32 on Friday.
